transcript.content: Hello, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, nice to meet you too. Um, honestly, what finally pushed me to come in is that... well, my shoulders and neck just stay clenched all day long. I teach preschool, and it feels like I'm constantly bracing for a classroom observation that never ends. And by the time evening rolls around, my jaw aches so badly that I can hardly even enjoy playing my guitar. It's just constant.
Besides classroom observations, do you find yourself worrying excessively about several other areas of your life?

Yeah, I do. It’s... well, my mind just keeps circling. I'll start thinking about whether I'll ever get hired again if I lose my job, or if I've somehow ruined my reputation with the parents. And then it shifts to my future, like whether retirement is just completely slipping away from me at this point. 

It even gets down to the really minor stuff. Like, if I make a small mistake during a story-time activity, I'll start worrying that it means I shouldn't even be trusted with children anymore. I just can't seem to turn it off.
How long have you been experiencing this pattern of excessive worry?
It's been going on for... well, I'd say about a year and two months now. It all really started back when I was fired from the preschool I used to work at.
Since you were fired, has your excessive worry continued during periods when there was no major work-related stressor?

I'm not really sure, to be honest. It... well, I don't think I've really had a period without some kind of stressor since then. It just feels like one long, continuous stretch of worrying. So I haven't really noticed a time when things were completely calm to even compare it to.
Before you were fired from the preschool, were you already experiencing this same pattern of excessive worry?

No, not really. I mean, I'd get stressed sometimes, like anyone would, but it wasn't like this. The constant, everyday worrying didn't really start until after I lost that job. Before that, things were pretty manageable.
Is the stress related to being fired—or its ongoing consequences—still actively affecting your life right now?

Yes, I'd say it definitely is. I mean... the whole situation with losing the job, it just sort of derailed everything. So, yeah, the fallout from it is still very much present and... affecting my everyday life right now. It hasn't really stopped.
On most days, how difficult is it for you to control or stop the worrying once it begins?

It's very difficult. I mean, once it starts, I really can't seem to stop it. I try telling myself to do something else—make a list, say a prayer, go out and weed the garden, or just focus on the next practical step I need to take. But it doesn't work. One worry just hands off to another, and before I know it, I've lost half the afternoon just sitting there, completely caught up in it.
On days when nothing related to losing your job or its aftermath is happening, do you still spend much of the day worrying excessively about unrelated areas of your life?

Well, yes. Even if it's a quiet day and nothing is actively happening, my mind just keeps circling. It goes from worrying about whether I'll ever get hired again, to... well, whether I've completely ruined my reputation with the parents. Then I start thinking about how my retirement is slipping away. It even gets to the point where I obsess over old things, like... wondering if a small mistake I made during a story-time activity means I just shouldn't be trusted with children anymore. It just jumps from one thing to another all day, no matter what else is going on.
Do you often have trouble sleeping because of your worrying?

Yes, I do. Most nights, I just lie in bed for hours... replaying interview answers, worrying about bills, or going over licensing forms in my head. It's really hard to shut it off. And even when I do finally manage to get some sleep, I almost always wake up around four in the morning. The second my eyes open, I'm already tense, just calculating everything that could go wrong that day.
If the job loss and its consequences were fully resolved tomorrow, do you think your excessive worrying would still continue across other areas of your life?

I... I honestly don't know. It's hard to even imagine that right now. The job situation is just so overwhelming that I can't really picture what it would be like if it were all fixed tomorrow. 

I'm not sure if my mind would just find something else to latch onto, or if I'd actually be able to relax for once. I just... I really couldn't say for sure what would happen.
Since the firing, has there been any period when its consequences were no longer actively affecting your life, even temporarily?
No, there hasn't been. It's been a constant issue since it happened. There hasn't been a single day or even a brief period where I wasn't dealing with the fallout in some way.
Compared with what has actually happened since you lost your job, how excessive or disproportionate does your level of worry feel to you?

I'm not really sure how to answer that, to be honest. I mean... losing my job was a massive blow, so the things I'm worrying about are real problems. I don't know if the amount I'm worrying is excessive or out of proportion. I haven't really thought about it like that. It just feels like... well, it just feels like my reality right now.
When you worry about retirement, making mistakes, or other parts of your life, do those worries feel directly connected to losing your job, or do they arise independently of that situation?

I think they feel pretty connected. Or at least, they all just kind of bleed into one another. 

My mind just keeps circling, you know? I mean, I'll start by agonizing over whether I'll ever get hired again... and then that turns into worrying about whether I've completely ruined my reputation with the parents. Then from there, I start thinking about how my retirement is just slipping away. It even gets to the point where I'm stressing over things like... wondering if a small mistake I made during a story-time activity means I shouldn't even be trusted with children anymore. 

So, yeah, it all feels tied back to the same situation. One worry just feeds right into the next.
Do you ever have excessive worry about topics that have no connection at all to losing your job or its consequences?

No, not really. I can't think of anything. Pretty much everything that keeps me up at night traces back to being fired. It's just... that one event has taken over everything, so I don't really have any major worries right now that are completely unrelated to it.
